title: Two copies of one prompt: a startup heal decides which one the model reads
aria: Tunatutor keeps its main prompt in two copies: a constant in code and a database row that a seed script and an admin screen can write. At every startup a heal compares the row with the code copy and resets it unless a person edited it, then each process caches the text, renders it on every turn and sends it to the model. Golden tests read only the code copy, so they stayed green in July 2026 while the model read an old row without rules 14 and 15.

build.title: The prompt text has three writers
build.text: The seed SQL and the admin screen write the database. The code copy, `DEFAULT_LAYER1_TEMPLATE`, holds 15 numbered rules and 8 slots and is reviewed in git.

build.title: The database holds a second copy
build.text: The row `ai-tutor-layer1` in `prompt_templates` is what the app prefers. In July the seed wrote an old copy without rules 14 and 15. Every admin save first archives the old text.

build.title: A startup heal picks one copy
build.text: At every startup the app compares the row with the code copy. With 0 archive rows the code copy wins; with 1 or more the admin's edit stays. The reset writes no archive row.

build.title: Each turn reads the cache, not the table
build.text: Each process caches the text. Code fills the 8 slots and sends the whole prompt on every call. Only lesson notes carry a prompt version and model id.

build.title: Tests that pin the text, and one that would judge it
build.text: Golden tests render only the code copy, so they stayed green all July. An eval scores replies on fixed inputs; nobody scored LOM-86's change.

route.title: Register the code copy before reading anything
route.text: The app records the key `ai-tutor-layer1`, its default text in code and the 8 `{{name}}` slots that code fills. Engineers review this copy in git.

route.title: Load the database row into the cache
route.text: The row has the old text, without rules 14 and 15. Each process keeps it in memory. Before the fix, startup ended here and the row won.

route.title: Compare the cached text with the code copy
route.text: If the two are equal, there is nothing to heal. Here they differ, so the app must decide which copy wins.

route.title: Ask whether a person ever edited the row
route.text: Every admin save first copies the old text into an archive table. 0 archived versions means no person changed it, so the code copy wins.

route.title: Reset the row without writing an archive
route.text: The heal writes the code copy over the row and reloads the cache. It writes no archive row, which would make the row look edited and stop later heals.

route.title: Fill the slots and send the whole prompt on each turn
route.text: A session reads the rules from the cache once. On every turn code computes the 8 slot values, and the filled text with all 15 rules goes to the model.

route.title: Stamp the prompt version and model on the result
route.text: Tutor replies carry no stamp today. The lesson-note writer saves prompt "v1" and the model id in two columns, so a bad note can be traced months later.
